rules.sentence: Approximately 26% of patients with celiac disease present with peripheral or axial arthritis.[71]

Patients with an atypical presentation of celiac disease may have mild gastrointestinal complaints, with the predominant symptoms including anemia, dental enamel defects, osteoporosis, arthritis, increased aminotransferases, neurological symptoms, infertility, and several associated autoimmune diseases.
Articular manifestations of the disease can encompass peripheral arthritis, sacroiliitis, or spondylitis.[72]
The clinical presentation may include symmetric polyarthritis, sacroiliitis, and enthesitis.[73]
